Dear Ms. Winter and the NDSU Evaluation Committee,
North Dakota State University has built something rare — a land-grant research institution that serves 12,000 students across undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, professional, and online programs, conducts nationally recognized research, and remains rooted in the mission of transforming lives in Fargo and across the state. That breadth of student population, that range of program audiences, and that ambition to grow qualified prospective student inquiries while connecting media spend directly to enrollment outcomes — that is exactly the challenge Propellant Media was built for.
We are pleased to submit this Technical Proposal in response to RFP No. SRC000211 for NDSU Marketing Campaign Digital Media Services. Propellant Media is a Google Premier Partner (Top 3% of agencies in the United States), an NMSDC-certified Minority Business Enterprise, and a digitally-native enrollment marketing agency headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. For over ten years, we have partnered with universities — from large public research institutions to community colleges — building full-funnel, data-integrated media infrastructure that connects the first impression to the enrolled student.
We understand NDSU's Marketing and Communications team manages brand strategy and creative direction, and that you are seeking an external partner to provide strategic media counsel, paid media execution, and measurement architecture that integrates with your TargetX (Salesforce) CRM. That is precisely the role we fill — strategic partner alongside your internal team, not a replacement for it.
Why Propellant Media for NDSU:
10+ years higher education enrollment marketing — from Kennesaw State University (7-year partnership, record enrollment of 45,000+ students) to Utah State University, Stevens Institute of Technology, University of Arizona, and more
Google Premier Partner — Top 3% of agencies nationally, with direct Google support, beta product access, and advanced attribution capabilities unavailable to standard partners
TargetX / Salesforce CRM integration experience — we have connected campaign attribution to the Salesforce ecosystem, enabling enrollment teams to trace every enrolled student to their originating campaign, channel, and creative
NMSDC Federally Certified MBE — diversity supplier credentials that align with NDSU's institutional values
Dedicated named team model — the team introduced in this proposal executes this engagement. No senior staff used to win and junior staff substituted post-award
Real-time Looker Studio dashboards — NDSU's marketing and enrollment teams get 24/7 live access to campaign performance, not monthly PDF reports
Contact information for this proposal:

Propellant Media is a full-service digital advertising agency headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with a second office in Charlotte, North Carolina. Founded in 2015 by CEO Justin Croxton, the firm has grown to a team of 25 professionals serving higher education, government, healthcare, and workforce development clients across the United States.
Our core service lines include paid search (Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising), paid social media (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn), programmatic display, OTT/CTV streaming, geofencing and location-based targeting, CRM integration, analytics, and enrollment attribution.
We hold two certifications that directly benefit Wor-Wic Community College:
Google Premier Partner -- Awarded to the top 3% of agencies in the United States based on client performance, ad spend, and certification standards.
Federally Certified MBE -- Certified through the National Minority Supplier Development Council (NMSDC), supporting Wor-Wic's supplier diversity objectives.
Today, Propellant Media manages digital campaigns for community colleges, four-year universities, government agencies, and workforce programs. Our flagship higher education engagement -- Kennesaw State University -- has spanned seven years and generated over 44,000 qualified student leads annually, contributing to record enrollment growth.

Propellant Media's community college practice is built on institutions with defined service areas, open-access admissions, and enrollment cycles that closely mirror Wor-Wic's. While our portfolio spans institutions nationally, our geofencing and audience segmentation methodology is purpose-built for bounded geographic markets — three-county service areas, defined high school feeder systems, and local employer ecosystems — exactly the environment Wor-Wic operates within. Our work at the Community College of Aurora serves a similarly defined metro service area where no other community college competes directly. That operational model — one community college, one geography, multiple audience segments — is the same model we bring to Wor-Wic's tri-county footprint on Maryland's Eastern Shore.

Team Composition and Roles
Project Manager (Team Member - Cris Burkhart)
Timeline Management: Utilizes Monday.com to monitor project progress, ensuring timely completion of tasks.
Workflow Coordination: Collaborates with Wor-Wic Community College’s Integrated Marketing team to streamline processes.
Milestone Reporting: Provides regular updates on project milestones and promptly addresses any logistical challenges.
Currently overseeing accounts such as Kennesaw State University, Life University.
Our tool of choice for project management is Monday.com, which allows us to project manage all of our major enterprise accounts.  See sample screenshot below.
Media Planner/Account Manager (Alyssa Dixon, Brent LeVasseur)
Primary Liaison: Serves as the main point of contact between Wor-Wic Community College and Propellant Media, ensuring clear and consistent communication.
Omnichannel Strategy Development: Crafts comprehensive media plans across platforms such as Google Ads, Meta (Facebook/Instagram), and programmatic.
Budget Allocation: Optimizes ad spend to maximize ROI while effectively reaching Wor-Wic Community College’s target audiences.
Performance Optimization: Continuously analyzes campaign data to refine strategies and improve outcomes.
Strategic Oversight: Aligns campaign strategies with Wor-Wic Community College’s objectives, overseeing execution and performance.
Quality Assurance: Ensures all deliverables meet the highest standards and align with Wor-Wic Community College’s brand identity.
Currently working with Kennesaw State University, Stevens Tech, Florida Gulf Coast, and Arizona State University.
Google Ads and Meta Specialist (Juan Gomez, Justin Croxton)
Campaign Management: Oversees the creation, execution, and optimization of campaigns on Google Ads and Meta platforms.
Keyword and Audience Research: Conducts in-depth research to identify high-performing keywords and target audiences.
Ad Performance Analysis: Monitors and analyzes ad performance metrics, making data-driven adjustments to enhance effectiveness.
Currently working with Kennesaw State University.
Analytics, Data Integration & Reporting Specialist (Aaron King)
Data Mapping & Integration: Implements robust tracking systems to monitor campaign performance across all platforms.
Comprehensive Reporting: Prepares detailed reports on key performance indicators, providing insights into campaign effectiveness.
Strategic Recommendations: Offers data-driven suggestions for campaign optimization and future strategies.
CRM Integration: Pushing form submissions with digital attribution information into CRM so applicants and enrolled students can ultimately be tracked back to a marketing channel, source, campaign, keyword, etc.
Dashboard Integration: Syncing enriched form data with dashboard so we are not just reporting on pixel fires but also reporting on “source-of-truth” conversions.
Currently working with Kennesaw State University, Utah State University, and University of Arizona.
Assignment Process and Team Member Tenure (Justin Croxton, Brent LeVasseur)
Consistency and Continuity: We prioritize assigning team members to Wor-Wic Community College’s account for a minimum of 1-2 years to build strong relationships and a deep understanding of Wor-Wic Community College’s brand and objectives.
Onboarding and Training: Team members undergo comprehensive onboarding to familiarize themselves with Wor-Wic Community College’s brand, goals, and the higher education landscape.
Performance Monitoring: Regular evaluations ensure team members meet performance standards and contribute effectively to the university’s success.
Creative & Brand Asset Develop (Diana Woodruff)
Oversees the full creative lifecycle—from initial concept through production and delivery—for static display, HTML5, and video ad assets tailored to Wor-Wic Community College's target audiences.
Leads cross-functional collaboration between strategy, media, and design teams to align messaging with campaign objectives and ensure consistency with Wor-Wic Community College's brand guidelines.
Implements A/B testing frameworks and data-informed creative iterations to enhance engagement, improve click-through rates, and drive RFIs and conversions across channels.
Programmatic Display Campaign Development & Optimizations (Dylan Meetze)
Leads the planning, building, and deployment of Wor-Wic Community College's programmatic display campaigns, leveraging audience segments, geotargeting, and dynamic creatives.
Continuously monitors and optimizes campaigns in real time—adjusting bids, refining placements, and reallocating spend based on performance trends and lead quality metrics.Collaborates closely with analytics and creative teams to insights into actionable enhancements that increase CTR, lower CPL, and improve overall campaign efficiency.
Alyssa Dixon will serve as Wor-Wic's dedicated Account Manager -- the single point of contact for campaign planning, performance updates, and strategic discussions. She is available via email, phone, and video conference during business hours with a guaranteed response time of 24 hours or less.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Midway through Year 2, we identified that Google Ads campaigns targeting transfer students were generating high click volume but low application completions.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">We narrowed geographic targeting to the 15-mile radius around Atlanta-area community colleges, rewrote ad copy to emphasize transfer credit acceptance and scholarship eligibility, and shifted the bid strategy to target CPA optimized for completed applications.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="40" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Within 60 days, transfer student applications from paid search increased 41% while cost per application dropped by 28%.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">KSU and Wor-Wic operate in different contexts -- KSU is a large four-year university, Wor-Wic is a community college serving three Maryland Eastern Shore counties. But the underlying challenges are identical: connecting digital campaigns to enrollment outcomes, optimizing the budget across multiple channels, reaching both traditional-age and adult learner audiences, and building real-time reporting that gives the marketing director full visibility into performance.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">The CRM integration framework we built at KSU -- tracking, audience mirroring, and enrollment attribution -- is the same framework we will deploy with Wor-Wic's Ellucian Colleague CRM Recruit. The Looker Studio dashboards KSU uses daily are the same platform Wor-Wic already has in place. The methodology transfers directly.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Asheville-Buncombe Technical Community College, in partnership with Forsyth Technical and Stanly Community Colleges, needed to drive enrollment for newly developed behavioral health certificate and AAS programs funded by a North Carolina state workforce grant. The challenge had three layers:
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Adult learner targeting: The primary audience was adults aged 30-40, including DSP workers, public safety professionals, and career changers entering human services fields -- not traditional college-age students.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Multi-campus, multi-county coordination: Campaigns had to be tailored across five distinct counties (Buncombe, Madison, Forsyth, Surry, and Stanly) with different labor markets and demographics.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Grant-cycle timeline: Results had to be delivered within defined grant phases aligned to a July-June fiscal year, with real-time reporting to coalition stakeholders.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Google Search: Captured high-intent queries like 'mental health training near me,' 'behavioral health certification,' and 'community college programs for public safety workers.' Campaigns were geofenced to each of the five target counties.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="40" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Inquiry volume from adults 30-40 increased 38% within four weeks of the creative shift, with no increase in media spend.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">AB Tech and Wor-Wic share a core challenge: reaching adult learners, career changers, and workforce credential seekers who are not actively searching for 'community college.' Both institutions serve regional labor markets where geofencing employer locations and workforce centers produces higher-intent leads than broad digital targeting. The Looker Studio dashboard infrastructure we built for AB Tech's coalition is the same platform Wor-Wic already uses -- and the multi-county geographic targeting mirrors the Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset county approach Wor-Wic needs.

The frustrations were specific and urgent:
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Low lead volume and high CPL: Prior campaigns were generating minimal inquiries at unsustainable cost.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">No transparency: The previous agency provided limited reporting, making it impossible for the nursing program to understand where the budget was being spent or which campaigns were working.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Within the first week, we identified that geofencing community colleges was producing the lowest-cost, highest-intent leads -- ADN students exploring BSN transfer options.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">We reallocated 20% of the hospital geofencing budget to expand community college targeting, adding 8 additional locations.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="40" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">CPL from community college geofencing dropped to $4.50 while maintaining lead quality, making it the most efficient channel in the entire campaign.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">This case study demonstrates two capabilities directly relevant to Wor-Wic's needs. First, geofencing precision: we targeted specific physical locations (hospitals, community colleges, competitors) and generated high-quality leads at a $6-9 CPL in just two weeks. Wor-Wic's RFP specifically calls for geofencing of area high schools, workforce centers, and community events -- the same methodology, applied to Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Second, agency transition: the University of Arizona came to us after a frustrating experience with a prior vendor. Wor-Wic's addendum reveals a similar dynamic -- the college has worked with the same vendor for four years and wants to expand capabilities. We know how to pick up where another agency left off, establish transparency from day one, and deliver measurable improvement quickly.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="0" w:afterAutospacing="0" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">We shifted 30% of the Meta budget from brand awareness creative to program-specific carousels and added bilingual versions for the five highest-demand workforce programs.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="40" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:ind w:left="720" w:hanging="360"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:u w:val="none"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Cost per inquiry dropped 22% within three weeks while inquiry volume increased -- proving that specificity beats generality in community college enrollment marketing.

<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="60" w:before="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:color w:val="e63412"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:b w:val="1"/><w:bCs w:val="1"/><w:color w:val="e63412"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">Why This Case Study Matters for Wor-Wic
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">CCA is the most directly comparable institution to Wor-Wic in Propellant Media's portfolio. Both are community colleges serving defined geographic service areas. Both need to reach diverse audiences including high school graduates, adult learners, workforce credential seekers, and dual enrollment families. Both compete against online national programs targeting the same adult learners with aggressive digital spend.
<w:left w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:bottom w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:right w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/><w:between w:color="auto" w:space="0" w:sz="0" w:val="none"/></w:pBdr><w:spacing w:after="100" w:lineRule="auto"/><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidDel="00000000" w:rsidR="00000000" w:rsidRPr="00000000"><w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Poppins" w:cs="Poppins" w:eastAsia="Poppins" w:hAnsi="Poppins"/><w:sz w:val="20"/><w:szCs w:val="20"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">The results speak for themselves: 63% enrollment growth is not incremental improvement -- it is transformational. The same methodology -- Google Ads for high-intent capture, Meta for lead generation at scale, programmatic geofencing for hyperlocal reach, site retargeting for conversion, and Looker Studio dashboards for real-time visibility -- is exactly what we will deploy for Wor-Wic across Wicomico, Worcester, and Somerset counties starting July 1, 2026.

Propellant Media does not absorb unspent budget, does not roll it into other campaigns without written approval from the marketing director, and does not carry balances forward without explicit direction from Wor-Wic's team. Every dollar is accounted for in the monthly reconciliation report.
Media spend on platforms automatically feed into dashboards for quick and easier spot checking and budget reconciliation.  If a client asks for monthly spend directly from the platform, we can supply that, as well. SNHU, WGU, and Purdue Global actively target adult learners aged 25–45 in the tri-county area. Wor-Wic's affordability and local presence are powerful counter-messages — but only if they're being distributed digitally.

w:val="26"/><w:rtl w:val="0"/></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve">d.12  Specific Deliverables & Project Timeline
The timeline below covers the full contract year from June 12, 2026 (contract award) through June 30, 2027 (end of FY2027), aligned directly to the eight campaign priorities Wor-Wic identified in the RFP. Wor-Wic's marketing director will have access to this same timeline in Propellant Media's Monday.com project workspace from Day 1.
Onboarding Phase — June 12 to June 30, 2026
There are 19 days between contract execution on June 12 and the July 1 service start. That window is fully structured. The incumbent agency's contract ends June 30 — Propellant Media will be fully operational and the Fall 2026 enrollment campaign will be approved and ready to launch before that contract expires. There is no gap and no ramp-up period that costs Wor-Wic time from its highest-enrollment-impact campaign of the year.
